examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Trace block identities and set conflicts before applying LRU or write rules. Write-through updates memory on a hit; write-back marks a line dirty and writes it when evicted. Write-allocate and no-write-allocate govern misses independently of the write-hit policy. A read miss can evict a dirty block under write-back.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A two-line fully associative LRU cache starts empty. For block references A,B,A,C,B, how many misses occur?

**Answer: 4.** A misses, B misses, A hits and becomes most recent. C misses and evicts B. The final B misses and evicts A. Total four misses. Counting distinct blocks alone would incorrectly give three.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
For a set-associative cache, LRU ordering is maintained within each set, not globally across unrelated sets.

A cache hit ratio alone does not determine memory write traffic.
